test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 14 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A cylindrical bucket of height 150 cm and radius 50 cm is full of water. A person wants to fill spherical balloons of radius 5 cm each with the water in the bucket. How many balloons can he fill completely with the water present in the bucket?
solution:
**Given:**

A cylindrical bucket of height 150 cm and radius 50 cm is full of water.

It is needed to be filled with some spherical balloons of the radius of 5 each

**Concept used:**

Volume of a cylinder = πr²h

Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr³

r = radius of sphere and base of the cylinder

h = height

**Calculation:**

Let n number of spherical balloons be required

According to the question,

π × 50² × 150 = (4/3) × π × 5³ × n

⇒ 2500 × 150 = (4/3) × 125n

⇒ 20 × 150 = (4/3)n

⇒ 3000 = (4/3)n

⇒ n = (3/4) × 3000

⇒ n = 2250

So, a total of 2250 balloons are required

**∴ 2250 balloons can he fill completely with the water present in the bucket.**
